thread:
sam: Heads-up: Found three related Go CVEs affecting grpc, oauth/jwt and net/http routing. CVE-2026-3344 (grpc), CVE-2026-3377 (oauth/jwt), CVE-2026-3390 (net/http request smuggling). Attaching quick notes and suggested pins.

lara: thanks. any exploit PoC yet?

ethan: I skimmed the advisories — grpc CVE is a deserialization boundary issue, requires crafted metadata. oauth/jwt is token parsing edge case (claims verification bypass in older libs). net/http looks like a header parsing quirk in specific proxy combos. No widespread PoC reported.

karina: impact matrix? which services use these modules directly vs transitively?

sam: quick breakdown:
- grpc (google.golang.org/grpc) used directly in inference-control, runtime, and some internal admin services.
- oauth/jwt (github.com/golang-jwt/jwt) used in authn middleware and a few CLI tools.
- net/http vulnerability surfaces when requests pass through our legacy edge proxy + custom header rewrite lib (edge-proxy-v1).

ethan: exploitability ranking (0-5): grpc 3, jwt 4, net/http 2. jwt higher because it can allow token forgery in certain parsing paths.

ben-sre: Do we have any public endpoints where jwt parsing happens on unauthenticated inputs?

karina: authn middleware is fronting /api/auth/* and /internal/token-introspect. Those are internal but exposed to customers on Dedicated. Risk is higher for Dedicated/private.

sam: suggested immediate actions:
1) Pin and patch jwt to v4.2.1 (fixes parser) in go.mod, run unit + integration tests.
2) grpc bump to v1.50.3 (security patch) and run canary on runtime-serving.
3) Add header normalization + unit test for edge-proxy to mitigate net/http quirk.
4) Create short-lived rule in WAF to block suspicious multi-header patterns until deploy.

lara: can we hotpatch runtime-serving without disrupting KV cache/LLM sessions?

ethan: plan: build grpc binary with new deps, run on a small dedicated pool (canary 5%), route a subset of inference traffic by tag -> monitor latency + error rate. Rolling back is just pointing service tag back. Should not disrupt KV caches since binary ABI unchanged.

ben-sre: deploy-bot: create canary job/PR?

deploy-bot: New canary job created: pipeline #sec-2081-canary. Targets: runtime-serving pool alpha-5. Notifies channel on failure.

karina: tests to add: jwt fuzz for claim parsing, grpc metadata boundary tests, and proxy header normalization unit tests. Also add integration smoke that signs and verifies tokens using both old and new libs.

sam: code snippet for go.mod replace for jwt:
```
require github.com/golang-jwt/jwt v4.2.1
replace github.com/golang-jwt/jwt => github.com/golang-jwt/jwt v4.2.1
```

ethan: grpc patch in go.mod:
```
require google.golang.org/grpc v1.50.3
```

karina: for net/http, quick mitigation in edge-proxy: normalize multiple headers by collapsing into first value and drop empty-values. I'll open a tiny PR.

lara: who's owning the rollout and SLO watch?

sam: owners:
- jwt: karina (auth)
- grpc: ethan (runtime) with ben-sre for deploy ops
- net/http/proxy: karina + infra team (edge-proxy)

ben-sre: I'll set up dashboards: token-failures, 5xx by service, unusual header counts. Alert thresholds: token-fail > 0.5% sustained over 5m.

ethan: timeline proposal: patch PRs by EOD today, canary deploy tomorrow morning, full rollout 24-48h after canary if stable. Backport to LTS branches as needed.

sam: prioritize jwt first (highest exploit risk), then grpc, then proxy mitigation.

karina: agree. will open PR now for jwt pin + tests. assigning to @karina.

lar a: one more ask — add audit log entries for token verification failures to make post-incident analysis easier. That helps detect silent bypasses.

sam: good call. can you add a short migration to enable structured token-failure logs?

karina: yes, will include structured logging in PR.

ben-sre: I'll coordinate WAF rule with infra and enable it as temporary protection during rollout.

deploy-bot: pipeline #sec-2081-canary queued. PR links: https://git.redwood/infradev/runtime/pulls/452, https://git.redwood/auth/pulls/210, https://git.redwood/edge-proxy/pulls/98

ethan: fyi runbook update: add CVE IDs + rollback steps in incident runbook (auth and runtime sections). I'll update after PRs land.

sam: ok team — action items summary in one place:
- karina: PR jwt pin + tests + structured logs (due EOD).
- ethan: PR grpc bump + canary plan + runbook update (due EOD).
- karina + infra: edge-proxy header normalization PR + unit tests (ASAP).
- ben-sre: dashboards, WAF rule, coordinate canary (tomorrow morning).
- sam: coordinate customer comms if Dedicated customers impacted.

lara: thanks all. ping here when canary metrics are live. :thumbsup:

sam: I'll update the ticket SEC-2026-87 with status and link PRs. Closing thread once rollouts complete.
